## Maintainer ruling recorded — Option A: extract the resolution half as a shared hook

Provenance: maintainer, 2026-08-27, PM chat decision-inbox batch 1 (adjudication session `session_01DKWDdUJ2XNRESVVWUvcpnh`), verbatim: 「同意，并继续」 — accepting the triage recommendation (2026-08-26T03:50Z facet block) as presented.

Ruled: extract the settled-schema RESOLUTION half as a shared hook exported from `@object-ui/react` — the `{ key, def } | null` state, keyed readiness, settle-on-every-exit shape — declared explicitly as a public-surface widening. Gate PLACEMENT stays per-component (`ObjectCalendar`'s provider-branch gate and its `dataConfig.object ?? schema.objectName` key are component-private truth, per this card's own measurement). Migration of the existing copies rides subsequent cards touching those components — ⛔ no one-shot four-package refactor. The four ungated views get per-component measurement before any gating; blanket gating (option C) stays excluded.

Dispatch notes: **Clause-②: yes** — a new published export widens the public surface; contract-review tier applies at dispatch. #6481 is re-priced to adopt the hook (keyed readiness) instead of writing a fourth hand copy, and stays `pm:blocked` on this card until the hook lands.

State: `needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue`.

Claim: `domain:ui` @ objectui PM seat, session `8ca04858-ea8e-5b85-9182-de59aa49e00c` — branch `claude/issue-6482-settled-schema-hook`.

Dispatching on the maintainer's 2026-08-27 ruling (「同意，并继续」), **Option A**, unchanged. Recording the three constraints the ruling attaches, because each one is a place a dev would naturally overreach:

1. ⛔ **Only the RESOLUTION half is extracted.** The `{ key, def } | null` state, keyed readiness, settle-on-every-exit shape. **Gate placement stays per-component** — `ObjectCalendar`'s provider-branch gate and its `dataConfig.object ?? schema.objectName` key are component-private truth, established by this card's own measurement. ⭐ That split is not a compromise; it is the measured boundary. Extracting the gate half too would be the wrong refactor, because an inline `value` data set issues no metadata read at all and a whole-effect gate would hold its query open on a resolution nothing was going to produce.
2. ⛔ **No one-shot four-package refactor.** Migration of the existing copies **rides subsequent cards** that touch those components. This dispatch lands the hook, not the migration.
3. ⛔ **No blanket gating of the four ungated views.** Option C was excluded on measurement: the cost of not gating is *not* uniform — `ObjectCalendar` measured a three-step paint when the schema read was slower, `ObjectKanban` measured a discarded round trip when it was faster. Gating is a **per-component** measurement, and those get their own cards afterwards.

**Clause-② yes** — a new published export widens `@object-ui/react`'s public surface. Contract-review tier; the widening is declared explicitly in the PR body, ⛔ never slipped in. Changeset `minor`. ⛔ No `needs:contract-review` label (phantom here, zero readers).

⭐ **This card unblocks #6481.** Per the ruling, #6481 is re-priced to adopt the hook (keyed readiness) instead of writing a fourth hand copy, and stays `pm:blocked` on this one until the hook lands. That is the whole point of the card: `ObjectTree` used two independent pieces of state (`objectSchema` plus a bare `schemaSettled` boolean), which **structurally cannot express keyed readiness** — and that is the root cause of #6481's stale `$expand` query. A shared hook makes "keyed by object" impossible to omit rather than merely conventional.

⇒ So the acceptance bar is not "a hook exists." It is: **the hook's shape must make #6481's defect unwritable.** A hook a caller can hold wrong reproduces the hand-copy problem with extra steps.

ACCEPT — PR #6690, head `877944237`, flipped ready; auto-merge once its table is green.

All three of the ruling's hard limits held: **gate placement stayed per-component**, ⛔ **no hand copy was migrated** (kanban / view / calendar / tree untouched), ⛔ **no blanket gating** of the four ungated views. The dispatch asked for the hook, and the hook is what came back.

## ⭐ The acceptance bar was "make #6481's defect unwritable", and it was met structurally

I said a hook a caller can hold wrong just reproduces the hand-copy problem with extra steps. The answer:

> the hook holds **one** piece of state and derives readiness **at render time** by comparing the settled key against the current key

That is the fix at the level the card was actually about. `ObjectTree`'s bug exists because it expressed readiness with **two independent pieces of state** (`objectSchema` plus a bare `schemaSettled`), which cannot represent "settled, but for a *different* key." With one state and a render-derived comparison there is no second variable to fall out of sync — **unwritable rather than merely avoided**, and demonstrated by a dedicated test plus a mutation ablation rather than asserted.

## ⭐⭐ The prediction missed, and reporting it honestly is the more useful result

Predicted: mutating `ready = resolution !== null && resolution.key === key` down to `ready = resolution !== null` (i.e. reproducing `ObjectTree`'s actual bug shape) turns **2 of 9** tests red.

Observed: **1 of 9**. The one that redded is the test modelled on #6481's real shape — settle a key successfully, *then* switch keys before the new fetch resolves. The second stayed green because it switches keys **before any resolution has ever settled**, so the base `resolution !== null` check already reads false under both the mutated and the original code.

⇒ ⭐ That is a fact about the suite's **discriminating power**, not a footnote: one of the two tests I would have counted as guarding the keyed-readiness property does not actually discriminate on that mutation. The dev *"recorded the actual observed direction rather than forcing the prediction"* — which is how the fact surfaced at all. A prediction quietly adjusted to match the run would have left a test in the file that looks like a guard and is not.

## Verification discipline worth naming

- ⭐ **Publication measured through the built entry, not an `export` keyword.** The dev loaded `dist/index.d.ts` through the TypeScript checker's `getExportsOfModule` — the same query `check-readme-exports.mjs` itself uses — with `useDataRefresh` as a **positive control** resolved through the identical query. Both true. That is exactly the "an `export` in a module file is not a published surface" rule, applied without being told twice.
- ⭐⭐ **`check:readme-exports` reported `PRECONDITION NOT MET`** (packagesRead 6 against a floor of 25 — sibling packages simply unbuilt in a fresh worktree) and was **reported literally**, ⛔ not booked as red and ⛔ not booked as green. Then, instead of stopping there, the dev measured what *could* be measured: the gate's own `scan()` invoked directly with the override mechanism its own fixture suite uses, scoped to `packages/react` — 0 fabricated, 0 wrong-path.
- ⭐ **`tsc --listFiles` confirmed `tsconfig.test.json` actually includes the new hook and its test** — the config claiming coverage and the program containing the file are two different facts.
- ⭐ Files were **`git add`ed before** `check:control-bytes` ran, so the new files were genuinely in the scanned population. An untracked new file is invisible to that scanner, which is the documented blind spot in #6545.
- ⭐ Restoration proven by an empty `git diff HEAD` **plus a byte-identical `git hash-object`** against the committed HEAD blob (`1d89c21a…`, matched before and after), under a trap anchored to an absolute `REPO_ROOT`.

Changeset `minor`; the public-surface widening is declared explicitly rather than slipped in, as clause-② requires.

## Next

⭐ **#6481 is now unblocked once this lands** — per the ruling it adopts `useSettledSchema` instead of writing a fourth hand copy. It stays `pm:blocked` until then. Migration of the existing three copies rides subsequent cards touching those components, ⛔ not a follow-up refactor card.
